removed.summary: Crown Princess Mette-Marit had been high patron of the Amandus Festival, a youth film festival in Lillehammer, since 2006.
removed.tie: Emails from 2011 to 2014 in the Epstein files show extensive contact between her and Epstein.
removed.consequence: On 28 April 2026 the festival's board voted unanimously to end the patronage, saying it had become "mer forstyrrende enn styrkende" (more disturbing than strengthening). She said she understood the decision.

removed.summary: Epstein's charity Gratitude America gave $57,897 in 2018 to this Paris nonprofit, which was launched the same year. POLITICO found it had barely existed beyond some basic paperwork.
removed.tie: Its president and treasurer were Jack Lang's former chiefs of staff, and Lang told POLITICO in October 2020 that the money was meant to finance a film.

removed.summary: Alexander Maxwell Djerassi has been a Djerassi trustee since 2017 and is now board secretary. An itinerary in the DOJ files lists him and fellow trustee Michael Molesky as guests at a "Mindshift Conference" on the weekend of 7 January 2011, with events on St. Thomas and on Epstein's island, Little St. James.
removed.tie: He is Ghislaine Maxwell's nephew, and he says of the 2011 lunch, speaking for himself and Molesky, "We had no awareness of Epstein's heinous crimes."
removed.consequence: Both men remain on the board. The residency calls the 2011 visit a "social lunch" years before they joined the board and says it had no ties to Epstein or Maxwell.

removed.summary: Harvard's May 2020 report found Epstein gave $9.1 million from 1998 to 2008, including $6.5 million in 2003 to create the Program for Evolutionary Dynamics (PED). Epstein visited PED's offices more than 40 times between 2010 and 2018.
removed.tie: Nowak, PED's director, kept a relationship with Epstein for 15 years, including after his release from prison, and gave him access to PED's offices.
removed.consequence: Harvard sanctioned Nowak in 2021 for breaking its rules on professional conduct, campus access and endorsements, and shut PED down. Harvard gave $200,937 in unspent funds to My Life My Choice and GEMS.

removed.summary: Jack Lang led the Institut du monde arabe from 2013. He is named 673 times in the DOJ files released on 30 January 2026, and emails show he travelled in Epstein's jet and car.
removed.tie: Lang, a former French culture minister, was introduced to Epstein by Woody Allen, called him "a generous sponsor" and exchanged messages with him from 2012 to 2019.
removed.consequence: Lang resigned as president on 7 February 2026. The day before, the Paris prosecutor had opened a preliminary investigation into him and his daughter Caroline for laundering of aggravated tax fraud. Both deny wrongdoing.

removed.summary: Steve Tisch is a LACMA trustee and in 2011 helped fund its purchase of Marclay's The Clock. Emails from April and May 2013 in the DOJ files show Epstein offering to introduce him to women.
removed.tie: Tisch says they had a "brief association" and emailed about adult women, movies, philanthropy and investments, that he never went to the island, and that he deeply regrets associating with Epstein.

removed.summary: Joi Ito wrote in an email that a $2 million gift from Bill Gates to the Media Lab was "directed by Jeffrey Epstein", while MIT's gift record said only that Gates gave on the recommendation of a friend who wished to remain anonymous. Gates's spokesperson says any claim that Epstein directed his grantmaking is "completely false".
removed.tie: Gates met Epstein at least once to discuss philanthropy, and media reports of flight records allege he flew on Epstein's jet from New Jersey to Palm Beach in March 2013.

removed.summary: MIT's Goodwin Procter review (January 2020) found Epstein gave MIT $850,000 in 10 gifts from 2002 to 2017, nine of them after his 2008 conviction, including $525,000 to the Media Lab under director Joi Ito. The New Yorker reported that Epstein arranged at least $7.5 million in donations to the Lab and that the Lab logged his gifts as anonymous, while MIT's donor database marked him "disqualified".
removed.tie: Ito solicited and accepted Epstein's post-conviction gifts to the Media Lab and hosted his visits, and he also took $1.2 million from Epstein for his own investment funds.
removed.consequence: Ito resigned on 7 September 2019. MIT committed $850,000 to survivor charities and put Seth Lloyd on paid leave.

removed.summary: Reid Hoffman met Epstein at the MIT Media Lab in July 2013, and in 2014 he went to Epstein's island for a fundraising event that Joi Ito says he requested. Their last known in-person meeting was a 2015 dinner Hoffman hosted, and Epstein emailed him in 2017.
removed.tie: Hoffman says he dealt with Epstein only for Media Lab fundraising.
removed.consequence: Hoffman apologised in September 2019 for having "helped to repair his reputation".

removed.summary: Chaslin was due to return to the Metropolitan Opera the next season after a 17-year absence. His emails with Epstein are in the DOJ files.
removed.tie: Chaslin is linked to at least 376 DOJ documents going back to 2012 and says his contact with Epstein was trivial.
removed.consequence: Slippedisc reported on 19 February 2026 that the Met withdrew its contract offer over the emails; it cites no statement from the Met.

removed.summary: The Metropolitan Opera was among the charities listed in the Jeffrey Epstein VI Foundation's press releases or IRS filings from 2010 to 2017. In July 2019 NBC News reported that the Met Opera was among 10 organisations with no record of any donation from Epstein or his foundation.
Peter Mahler sat on the Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra's 35-member board until February 2026. FOX6 first reported his Epstein link on 9 February 2026.
removed.tie: The Epstein files show Mahler worked as a recruiter for Epstein in 2013, when Epstein was looking for an assistant, and Mahler calls the allegations against Epstein "abhorrent".
removed.consequence: Mahler resigned from the board. On 13 February 2026 the orchestra said it had accepted his resignation and that the matter was unrelated to his board service.

removed.summary: In an 18 March 2012 email in the DOJ's January 2026 release, Epstein wrote that "the govt is going to open the musee dorsay for me and woody alien at 4", "alien" being his typo for Woody Allen. He later bragged about the visit in emails, including one to Eva Dubin.
removed.consequence: The Musée d'Orsay did not respond to ARTnews and has not confirmed the visit.

removed.summary: Black lent his Van Gogh "Quarry near Saint-Rémy", valued at $60 million in 2016, to the Orsay's 2014 show "Van Gogh/Artaud: Le Suicidé de la Société". The Art Newspaper reports that the Epstein files indicate his Van Goghs were collateral for large bank loans around 2016.
removed.tie: Epstein gave Black "extensive financial advice" for fees of at least $158 million, and Black denies wrongdoing and says he knew nothing of Epstein's crimes until 2019.

removed.summary: Eileen Guggenheim was the Academy's dean in 1995 and later its board chair. Emails show that after Epstein's 2008 conviction she encouraged his support of the school, and in 2014 he gave $30,000 for scholarships at her invitation.
removed.tie: Maria Farmer alleges that Guggenheim introduced her to Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell at her 1995 thesis show, pressed her to sell Epstein a painting at a steep discount and ignored her complaints; Guggenheim denies "the substance and odious implications" of the allegations.
removed.consequence: The Academy commissioned a report that disputed Farmer's claims. In March 2026 it said it should not have taken Epstein's money or let him attend events, and Guggenheim brought her retirement forward by a month, to April 2026.

removed.summary: Epstein sat on the Academy's board from 1987 to 1994 and met student Maria Farmer there in 1995; Farmer reported him to the FBI in 1996, the first report against him. After his 2008 conviction he bought a $25,000 table at the Academy's Tribeca Ball in 2012 and in 2014, gave $30,000 for scholarship support in 2014, and attended Academy events.
removed.consequence: In March 2026 the Academy admitted "serious failures", said it would give $65,900 linked to the 2012 and 2014 events to GEMS, and set up an ethics committee. It had given GEMS $30,000 in 2020.

removed.summary: Caroline Lang presided over Pictanovo's economic support fund for films and series until 4 February 2026. Pictanovo is an association funded by the Hauts-de-France region.
removed.tie: She co-owned Prytanee LLC, a US Virgin Islands company created in 2016, with Epstein, and an Epstein will document names her for $5 million.
removed.consequence: She stepped down on 4 February 2026 after the US Justice Department released the Epstein emails. France's National Financial Prosecutor (PNF) has opened a preliminary inquiry into her and Jack Lang on suspicion of laundering aggravated tax fraud.

removed.summary: Epstein's foundation Gratitude America gave $110,000 in 2016 to Verse Video Education, the nonprofit behind Elisa New's Poetry in America, and New and Epstein emailed about funding her projects from 2013 to at least 2018, including a possible $500,000 donation. Harvard gave the nonprofit office space and paid part of its staff salaries.
removed.tie: New, a former Harvard professor married to Larry Summers, told the Boston Globe she did not know about Harvard's 2008 ban on Epstein gifts when she took the 2016 donation.
removed.consequence: GBH ended its ties with the show in 2023, and PBS stopped distributing it in December 2025. Harvard opened an investigation into New and Summers.

removed.summary: Emails released in November 2025 show Epstein brokered a donation of an unspecified amount from Leon Black to Elisa New, which Harvard did not disclose. New wrote to Epstein in 2015 that "The Leon Black gift changed everything for me last year", tying it to her Poetry in America project.
removed.tie: Black paid Epstein $158 million from 2012 to 2017, according to a 2021 Dechert review for Apollo.
removed.consequence: PBS stopped distributing Poetry in America in December 2025.

removed.summary: Prince Andrew was the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra's patron, and the orchestra thanked him for his support "over the past 15 years". In November 2019 its board decided to "part company with its patron, with immediate effect".
removed.tie: A longtime friend of Epstein, he lost his royal titles in October 2025 and was arrested on 19 February 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office over what the Epstein files disclosed; he has not been charged.

removed.summary: In 2001, while David A. Ross was director, SFMOMA acquired a 20% interest in John F. Simon Jr.'s ComplexCity (2000), recorded as a "fractional and promised gift of Jeffrey Epstein". In 2009 director Neal Benezra wrote to thank Epstein for his "continued support".
removed.consequence: SFMOMA says the 2009 letter was standard donor language and it has no record of support from Epstein after 2001. The work was never exhibited; the museum deaccessioned it in October 2019 and returned its share to the artist.

removed.summary: Oxman's Vespers II was shown in her 2022 SFMOMA exhibition "Nature x Humanity". Emails in the 2026 DOJ release show she thanked Epstein in 2017 for supporting her Vespers "death masks", and in December 2017 he agreed by email to give $25,000 toward a follow-on project.
removed.tie: Epstein gave $125,000 to Oxman's MIT design lab in 2017, and she apologised in 2019.

removed.summary: Caroline Lang held roles at Séries Mania, the Lille TV-series festival. La Voix du Nord first reported that she had to give them up after the US Justice Department released Epstein's emails.
removed.tie: She held 50% of Prytanee LLC, a company created with Epstein in the US Virgin Islands in 2016, a will Epstein signed promised her $5 million, and she says Woody Allen introduced her to Epstein in 2012.
removed.consequence: She stood down on 4 February 2026, the same day she left Pictanovo. She calls Epstein an acquaintance and says she received no money or benefit.

removed.summary: Chaslin was engaged, without a formal signed contract, to conduct Verdi's "Aida" at Teatro Massimo from 22 to 31 May 2026. The DOJ files show a relationship with Epstein dating back to 2012.
removed.tie: Chaslin corresponded with Epstein from 2012, including about #MeToo, and in 2013 recommended an interpreter for Epstein's Paris museum visits.
removed.consequence: In March 2026 superintendent Marco Betta cancelled the engagement after the orchestra raised unease about Chaslin's ties to Epstein. Chaslin denies wrongdoing, says he "never received a single cent", and says a DOJ letter confirms he had no involvement.
